newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total says production high at H2 start.
newsitem.headline: Total says production high at H2 start.

text.p: French energy group Total SA said high production levels in the first half of the year, which contributed to a jump in its first-half results, were steady at the start of the second half.
The group also said in a statement that production and productivity growth in the medium term -- to the year 2000 -- would help increase its profitability.
But it gave no forecast for its 1996 full year results.
Its return on equity in the first half was 9.9 percent. The group aims for 10 percent in 1998, based on Brent prices of $16.40 per barrel and a rate of 5.27 francs to the dollar.
On those assumptions, its return in the first half of 1996 would have been 8.4 percent.

Its net attributable profit for the first half jumped 45 percent to 2.63 billion francs. Total said a favourable environment, including higher oil prices, had a positive impact on its operating results of around 700 million francs relative to the year-earlier period.
Refining margins were above the levels seen in the first half of 1995 but remain volatile, the group said.
The operating result of the group's energy production activity rose 53 percent to 3.3 billion francs.
Total attributed the gain to higher crude prices, a 15 percent rise in production to the equivalent of 766,000 barrels per day and a drop in technical costs.

The operating result of the refining-distribution business rose 65 percent to 674 million francs, helped by improved refining margins in Europe and efforts to push down the break-even level at its refineries, Total said.
The chemical business's operating result rose eight percent to 984 million francs on a 14.9 percent rise in sales. The rise was due to a contribution from Hutchinson and the paints unit.
